theme: Jeremiah buys a field; the Branch of David
readingInstruction: Read Jeremiah 32:1-33:26. While Babylon is besieging the city, God tells Jeremiah to buy a field. Read it as an act of faith. Then read the promise of the Branch and the covenant with David and the Levites.
settingTheScene: It is 587 BC, the tenth year of Zedekiah. Jerusalem is under siege, and Jeremiah is imprisoned in the court of the guard for predicting its fall. God tells him that his cousin will come and offer to sell him the family field at Anathoth, which is now in enemy territory. He buys it. The scene is among the most striking acts of faith in Scripture.
observation: “Buy my field that is at Anathoth, for you have the right of redemption by purchase” (32:7).
“I signed the deed, sealed it, got witnesses, and weighed the money on scales” (32:10).
“Ah, Lord GOD! It is you who have made the heavens and the earth by your great power… Nothing is too hard for you” (32:17).
“Behold, I am the LORD, the God of all flesh. Is anything too hard for me?” (32:27).
“I will make with them an everlasting covenant, that I will not turn away from doing good to them” (32:40).
“Fields shall be bought in this land of which you are saying, It is a desolation” (32:43).
“Call to me and I will answer you, and will tell you great and hidden things that you have not known” (33:3).
“In those days and at that time I will cause a righteous Branch to spring up for David” (33:15).
interpretation:
Jeremiah’s act is a visible sermon. The Babylonian army is at the gate. Anyone who buys land in the country is wasting money. But God says: buy it. The deed is signed, sealed, witnessed, and placed in a clay jar to last a long time. The meaning: “Houses and fields and vineyards shall again be bought in this land.” Jeremiah invests in a future he cannot see. His purchase is a pledge of God’s promise.

Afterward, Jeremiah prays, and he is honest about his confusion. “Behold, the siege mounds have come up to the city… and the city is given into the hands of the Chaldeans. What you spoke has come to pass, and behold, you see it. Yet you, O Lord GOD, have said to me, Buy the field.” How can both be true? God answers with a question: “Is anything too hard for me?” He confirms the judgment, but promises restoration. “I will gather them from all the countries.” He will give them one heart and one way, “that they may fear me forever.” And again the promise of the everlasting covenant, “that I will not turn away from doing good to them.”

Chapter 33 continues the theme from a prison. God says, “Call to me and I will answer you, and will tell you great and hidden things.” It is a promise to those who pray in impossible situations. The city will be healed and cleansed. The sounds of joy and gladness will return, “the voice of the bridegroom and the voice of the bride,” and of those who bring thank offerings.

The center is the promise of the Branch: “I will cause a righteous Branch to spring up for David.” The covenant with David will not fail. As sure as day and night, God’s promises stand. Even in the siege, Jeremiah’s hope is not in the army but in the word of God.
connection: Luke 1:37 says, “For nothing will be impossible with God,” echoing Jeremiah 32:17 and 27. Mark 10:27 says that all things are possible with God. Hebrews 11:1 says faith is the assurance of things hoped for. Jeremiah’s purchase of the field fits Ephesians 1:13-14, where the Spirit is the guarantee of our inheritance. Romans 4:17-21 describes Abraham believing against hope. Psalm 50:15 invites us to call on God in the day of trouble.
application:
Ask where God may be asking you to act in faith toward a future you cannot yet see.

Memorize Jeremiah 33:3 and pray it in a situation that seems impossible.

Pray the question, “Is anything too hard for the LORD?” for a specific need.
prayerPrompts: Tell God that nothing is too hard for him, and name the thing you have been afraid to ask.
Ask him to teach you to “buy fields” in faith, trusting his promises.
Thank him for the Branch of David.
